brief:
An oral history initiative has launched to preserve the memories of killed Palestinian journalists through voice notes from friends and colleagues, Middle East Eye reported. The project's website debut marks the first anniversary of Israeli forces killing Al Jazeera journalist Anas al-Sharif, whose death drew international attention to the risks Palestinian journalists face.

The platform documents the lives and professional work of Palestinian media workers lost during the conflict, capturing personal testimonies and recollections from those who knew them directly. By aggregating voice messages from friends rather than relying on traditional written obituaries or institutional statements, the project creates a distinctive archive that centers the voices of people closest to the deceased journalists.

title: Oral history project memorializes slain Palestinian journalists through voice messages
